match.reason: None of the bank points defines a market as a place or system where buyers and sellers trade and prices guide production; they cover market failure, business market types, target markets, marketing strategy and the marketing mix, which are different ideas or at a different depth.

draft.title: What a market is
card: A market is any place or system where buyers and sellers trade. It can be face to face, such as a farmers market, or online, such as a shopping website.
A market does not need one building or one location. What makes it a market is that buyers and sellers are able to trade with each other.
In a market, the amount buyers want and the amount sellers offer help set a price.
Prices send signals. A high price tells producers that buyers want more of a good, so they may make more. A low price may lead them to make less.
draft.remember: A market is where buyers and sellers trade, and its prices guide what is made.

a.q: Which of these is a market?
opts: An online site where people buy and sell used phones
A factory that makes phones for its own company
A household that makes its own meals each night
A government plan for how many phones to make
a.why: A market is any place or system where buyers and sellers trade, and an online site fits that. The factory is tempting, but it makes phones for its own use and no buyers and sellers trade there.
a.clue: Look for buyers and sellers trading, in any form.

b.q: Crowds at Mia's café in Geelong grow, so she can charge more for coffee. How does this price help guide what is made?
opts: It signals strong demand, so sellers may make more coffee
It signals weak demand, so sellers may make less coffee
It shows that coffee must now be sold in a single building
It tells buyers how much coffee the government wants made
b.why: A higher price signals that buyers want more of the good, so producers may make more. The second option reverses cause and effect, because a rising price does not point to weak demand.
b.clue: What does a higher price tell producers about what buyers want?

a.best: An online site where people buy and sell used phones

b.best: It signals strong demand, so sellers may make more coffee

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the 'weak demand' option 'the second option', but the options are shuffled and it is listed first here. Its claim that this option 'reverses cause and effect' is also inaccurate: the option reads the signal the wrong way round, which is not a cause-and-effect reversal. The why should name the option by its content and say it misreads the signal.
